text:
sam: FYI support ticket #INC-5821. Customer rotated their signing keys and started getting 401s from our API about 10m after rotation. They say tokens were issued by their auth provider with kid=key-v2 but our requests keep failing with 'kid not found' and 'signature verification failed'.

nina: @sam can you paste the exact error from our gateway logs and any headers from the failing request? Also want to know if they hit a Dedicated/private endpoint or hosted.

sam: Hosted. Logs below (redacted):
```
2026-03-14T15:12:02Z INFO auth: verifying token user=acme-app request_id=xyz123
2026-03-14T15:12:02Z WARN auth: jwk lookup kid=key-v2 not found in cache (cache_age=00:04:21)
2026-03-14T15:12:02Z ERROR auth: signature verification failed: kid not present in JWKS
```
Curl reproduction they ran (auth header token signed with kid=key-v2):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJS... (kid: key-v2)" https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete
```
They also sent the JWT header and it clearly had kid=key-v2.

arjun: Two likely causes: 1) JWKS cache TTL is relatively long and we don't proactively refresh on unknown kid, or 2) clock skew causing tokens to appear not-yet-valid or expired (should be an "iat/nbf/exp" mismatch). From the log snippet it looks like kid missing rather than exp. Does the JWKS fetch log show any 200/304 around that time?

sam: Here's JWKS fetch trace from the auth service (scrubbed):
```
2026-03-14T15:07:40Z DEBUG jwks: fetched https://idp.acme/jwks.json status=200 cache-control=max-age=300
2026-03-14T15:12:01Z DEBUG jwks: cache-valid (age=00:04:21), not refetching
```
So the idp rotated keys at 15:10 and responded to a new jwks.json with key-v2, but our service didn't fetch because cache was still within max-age. The idp didn't send cache invalidation headers.

nina: Ok that's the classic race between rotation and caching. We should avoid hard-failing on unknown kid without a refresh attempt. We also need to surface this to support so they can ask customers to stagger rotation.

maria: Quick question — do we have an existing fallback in the auth middleware (node/Go) to re-fetch JWKS on unknown kid? I thought we implemented a refresh-on-kid-miss pattern in the runtime but maybe it's not in the hosted variant.

arjun: We do in a couple places, but not everywhere. Current behavior: check cache -> if kid present verify -> else fail. Improvement: on kid-miss perform one immediate fetch of JWKS (non-blocking retries with backoff) and re-check. Also guard with a short-circuit TTL so we don't DDOS the idp during a large burst. Pseudocode: 
```
if (!jwks.has(kid)) {
  if (!recentRefreshInProgress) {
    fetch_jwks_immediate()
  }
  // re-check after fetch (synchronous wait up to 500ms) then continue
}
```
We should also log a metric when we see kid-miss so customer support can correlate.

support-bot: :rotating_light: New support ticket linked: #INC-5821 created (priority=P2) — assigned to sam.

sam: Customer impact: several hundred requests dropped over ~8 minutes, reporting errors from their integration tests. Immediate remediation options: (A) ask customer to rollback key rotation until we release a patch, (B) perform a forced JWKS refresh for hosted gateway (requires deploy), or (C) instruct customer to publish old key alongside new key for a rotation overlap window.

nina: For immediate triage we can do a hotfix that triggers a JWKS refresh on the gateway for that tenant only. That avoids global risk. Is there an admin endpoint we can call?

arjun: There's an internal admin endpoint on the auth service (/admin/refresh-jwks?issuer=...) but it's not exposed for hosted tenants by default. I can flip a flag in staging to test, then run it in prod for that issuer. Needs ops approval.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Deploy lock check OK. Maintenance window not required for one-off admin call.

sam: I'll coordinate with ops to run the admin refresh for issuer=https://idp.acme at 15:30 UTC. Meanwhile, can we produce a reliable repro in our sandbox? Steps I used:
1) In sandbox, configure auth middleware with cache-control=max-age=300 for jwks
2) Start service and fetch jwks (key-v1 present)
3) Update jwks.json on the idp to remove key-v1 and add key-v2
4) Immediately issue a token signed with key-v2 and call the API -> observe 401 and kid-miss log.

nina: Good. Can you paste the minimal curl + jwt generation steps so oncall can reproduce quickly?

sam: Minimal repro:
```
# on idp sandbox: replace jwks.json contents with new key
# generate token using private key for kid=key-v2
TOKEN=$(node gen_jwt.js --kid key-v2 --iss https://idp.sandbox --aud api)
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://sandbox-api.redwood.local/v1/complete
# expect 401 + log: jwk lookup kid=key-v2 not found
```
Also shared gen_jwt.js snippet (node jose lib) in the ticket.

arjun: Action items: 
- arjun: implement refresh-on-kid-miss in auth middleware (safe path + metric) and add a config toggle for strictMode. Deadline: EOD tomorrow.
- nina: open internal bug with steps, severity, and link to support ticket; add runbook steps for forced jwks refresh. Deadline: today COB.
- sam: coordinate one-off admin refresh for issuer=https://idp.acme and update the ticket with outcome. ETA: 15:35 UTC.
- maria: update docs for recommended rotation patterns (publish old key + overlap window) and include sample jwks rotation checklist. Deadline: 2 business days.

maria: I'll also add a short note to the onboarding docs about clock skew checks — some tokens had iat slightly in future for other customers in the past. Recommend checking NTP on their auth servers.

sam: After admins refreshed JWKS (15:32) the customer reported errors stopped. We captured metrics: kid-miss spike ~350 events between 15:10-15:18. No further 5xx/latency regressions.

nina: Good. Postmortem items: add metric, make refresh-on-kid-miss default in hosted runtimes, add tenant-scoped admin refresh API doc, and training for support on rotation Qs. Severity P2 -> convert to P1 if next rotation causes >5% drop in business-critical traffic.

arjun: Implementation note for reviewers: avoid always hitting issuer on every unknown kid — only 1 immediate fetch + short blocking wait (<=500ms) then background retries logged with rate limit. Also add a circuit breaker per-issuer.

sam: Filing the internal bug now and will link the support ticket. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
